paper_title: Phenol-Functionalized Perylene Bisimides as Amine-Free Electron Transporting Interlayers for Stable Nonfullerene Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What is the chemical structure of the PBI-2P cathode interlayer material and its champion power conversion efficiency (PCE)?
qa_pairs.answer: PBI-2P is composed of a perylene bisimide (PBI) core functionalized with two 2,6-di-tert-butylphenol units at the bay positions. When applied as a cathode interlayer in a PM6:Y6:PC71BM organic solar cell system, it achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 17.20%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Phenol-Functionalized Perylene Bisimides as Amine-Free Electron Transporting Interlayers for Stable Nonfullerene Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: How does the application of a PBI-2P interlayer affect the work function of a silver cathode and the resulting device performance?
qa_pairs.answer: The application of a PBI-2P interlayer reduces the work function (WF) of the silver (Ag) cathode from -4.58 eV to -3.81 eV. This significant decrease in the cathode's work function corresponds to an increase in the open-circuit voltage (Voc) of the organic solar cell device.
qa_pairs.source_title: Phenol-Functionalized Perylene Bisimides as Amine-Free Electron Transporting Interlayers for Stable Nonfullerene Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: Explain the chemical mechanism that leads to the enhanced conductivity of PBI-2P compared to its precursor PBI-2Br.
qa_pairs.answer: The enhanced conductivity of PBI-2P (2.98 x 10⁻⁵ S/cm compared to 0.96 x 10⁻⁵ S/cm for PBI-2Br) is attributed to the 2,6-di-tert-butylphenol groups. The electron-withdrawing effect on the para-position of the phenol enhances its acidity, facilitating deprotonation into phenolates and subsequent oxidation into stable radical and biradical species, which support charge transport.
qa_pairs.source_title: Phenol-Functionalized Perylene Bisimides as Amine-Free Electron Transporting Interlayers for Stable Nonfullerene Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: Compare the photostability of organic solar cells using PBI-2P interlayers to those using conventional amine-based interlayers like PFN-Br.
qa_pairs.answer: Devices utilizing PBI-2P exhibit superior photostability, maintaining 90% of their initial PCE (T90) for 12 days under continuous white-LED irradiation. In contrast, devices using amine-based interlayers such as PFN-Br, PDINO, and PEIE reach the same 10% decay point in approximately 6 days, demonstrating that the amine-free PBI-2P provides roughly double the stability duration.
qa_pairs.source_title: Phenol-Functionalized Perylene Bisimides as Amine-Free Electron Transporting Interlayers for Stable Nonfullerene Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: Why do amine-group containing interlayers cause instability when used with nonfullerene acceptors like Y6?
qa_pairs.answer: The instability is caused by a chemical reaction where electrons are transferred from the amine groups of the interlayer material to the dicyanomethylene indanone (IC) termini of the Y6 acceptor. This electron transfer process leads to the decomposition of the materials at the contact interface.
qa_pairs.source_title: Phenol-Functionalized Perylene Bisimides as Amine-Free Electron Transporting Interlayers for Stable Nonfullerene Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What are the processing advantages of PBI-2P regarding solvent choice and film thickness tolerance?
qa_pairs.answer: PBI-2P is highly soluble in polar alcohols like methanol (up to 20 mg/mL), allowing for solution processing without corroding the underlying active layer. Furthermore, it shows excellent thickness tolerance; a 20 nm thick layer maintains a PCE of 15.47%, whereas a PFN-Br layer of the same thickness causes the PCE to drop to 1.56% with an S-shaped J-V curve.
qa_pairs.source_title: Phenol-Functionalized Perylene Bisimides as Amine-Free Electron Transporting Interlayers for Stable Nonfullerene Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: According to transient photocurrent measurements, how does PBI-2P compare to PFN-Br and PDINO in terms of charge extraction?
qa_pairs.answer: PBI-2P interlayers facilitate significantly faster charge extraction than conventional interlayers. Transient photocurrent measurements show a decay time of 0.96 µs for PBI-2P, which is faster than the 1.34 µs observed for PFN-Br and the 1.24 µs observed for PDINO.
qa_pairs.source_title: Phenol-Functionalized Perylene Bisimides as Amine-Free Electron Transporting Interlayers for Stable Nonfullerene Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: How does the apparent electron mobility of a device with a PBI-2P interlayer compare to that of a neat Y6 film?
qa_pairs.answer: The apparent electron mobility of a device using a PBI-2P cathode interlayer is 6.24 x 10⁻³ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ as measured by SCLC. This is more than two orders of magnitude higher than the mobility of a neat Y6 film, which is only 3.75 x 10⁻⁵ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.
qa_pairs.source_title: Phenol-Functionalized Perylene Bisimides as Amine-Free Electron Transporting Interlayers for Stable Nonfullerene Organic Solar Cells
